title: fix(app-shell): a route's lazy view chunk loads beside the route reads, so it no longer holds the boot splash (objectui#12980, part 2)
body:
Part of #12980
Clause-②: no

Part 2 of the card, re-scoped by measurement (os-dev-report `6253703505`, seat ruling `6253719490`, claim `6253725595`). Wanted item 2 as written, "the chrome's dashboard and report reads hold the splash", was falsified: the splash never waited on them. The remaining delay was the route's own lazy view. #12980 remains open for item 3 and for part 1's leftovers.

## What changed

`AppContent` renders each route's view (page, dashboard, report, record, search, the metadata admin, the app designer, the marketplace) as a lazy chunk, under a `Suspense` whose fallback is the boot splash (`LoadingScreen`). Until now that chunk was requested only when the console chrome first rendered the route. The route therefore suspended at chrome commit even with the chunk cached. react-dom then holds a fallback it has just shown for its reveal throttle (`FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS`, 300 ms in react-dom 19.2.8), so the splash stayed about 0.27 s after the route's data was in.

- Each lazy route view is now a `preloadableLazy` element, spelled `routeChunk.lazy(() => import('...'))` so the declared-lazy-views ledger (`scripts/vite-declared-lazy-views.ts`) still reads every declaration. The matcher finds the same 15 relative specifiers before and after. Its `preload()` starts the import once, and a failed import may start again. An element whose chunk has resolved by its first render renders the view component directly and never suspends. One still in flight renders the lazy wrapper, under the same Suspense fallback as before. The choice is made once per mount, so a mounted route never swaps component type.
- `AppContent` looks up the route's view in an `APP_ROUTE_CHUNKS` table (route path to view), ranked with `matchRoutes` beside every path in `APP_ROUTE_METADATA_READS` and the host's extra routes. It starts that view's import in an effect keyed on the route, in parallel with the route's metadata reads. A path that resolves to an eagerly bundled element or to a host route starts nothing.
- The route reads part 1 settled are unchanged, and the fallback design is unchanged (see Acceptance notes).

## Trace: chrome commit to splash end, before / after

Rig: production `vite build` of the console (before: `024b7b6`; after: `a137fc7`), served by `vite preview` with its `/api` proxy pointed at a fake API that answers every call in 150 ms. Chromium via Playwright. Times are in-page `performance.now()` read by a top-frame MutationObserver; "blank" means no splash and no chrome after the splash was shown. Warm = a warm-up open, then 3 opens in the same page. Cold = 3 fresh browsers.

| route | before, warm | before, cold | after, warm | after, cold |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `page/welcome` | 273 / 271 / 280 ms | 251 / 108 / 141 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 ms |
| `dashboard/sales` | 180 / 148 / 134 ms | 251 / 248 / 249 ms | 0 / 91 / 87 ms | 111 / 147 / 123 ms |

No run shows a blank frame. On the page route, the splash now ends in the same commit as the chrome.

On the dashboard route, preloading starts the chunk import beside the route reads, but the import is still in flight when the chrome commits. An instrumented build (not committed) logged the preload start and its resolution: the `DashboardView` chunk graph took 450–520 ms to resolve, against route reads of one 150 ms wave (or 400 ms at a slower setting). The route view mounted as the lazy wrapper, then as the component once the import resolved. That residual is chunk loading, not the throttle on a cached chunk, which is the case the ruling's "change the fallback only if" names. I left the fallback design alone. Reading: the in-flight case is the CONTROL below, and it never draws a blank.

## Tests

- `AppContent.routeChunkPreload-12980.test.tsx` (real `AppContent` + `AuthProvider`; metadata buckets and view modules answer only when the test says so):
  - (a) A page route requests its chunk while the splash is up, before `meta/page` lands. Once the chunk and the reads are in, the page renders together with the chrome, and a MutationObserver sees no splash ever attached inside the chrome.
  - (b) CONTROL: when a route's metadata lands before its chunk, the route slot draws the splash (never a blank), then the view.
- `appRouteChunks-12980.test.ts` reads the `Route` table and `APP_ROUTE_CHUNKS` out of `AppContent.tsx` with the TypeScript parser. It fails on a lazy route view without its row, a row naming another view, or a row naming no route, with a positive control.
- Ablation at `47c9549` / `15bf8cd`: `objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the `preloadAppRouteChunk(appSubPath, hostRoutePaths);` call (anchor 1 to 0, blob `529827fce6d3` to `ec25cc21aa2d`). Unmutated: 2 passed. Mutated: (a) red (`expected false to be true` on the chunk-requested wait), (b) CONTROL green. Restored: blob `529827fce6d3` equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Verification (head `a137fc7`)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0 at `a84ee49`. After that, only an unused test helper was removed, and the new tests were re-run at `a137fc7`: 5 passed. Closure build `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...`: 28/28, all cached.
- vitest `--maxWorkers=1` under the shared lock: `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/` + `useNavigationSync*` + `AppHeader*` + `scripts/__tests__/vite-declared-lazy-views.test.ts` + `check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts`: 71 files, 724 tests passed. The full `packages/app-shell/` directory is declared to CI.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` narrowed to the 3 changed source files (the population is the changed lintable files; 3 files in the JSON report). 0 errors. `AppContent.tsx` keeps the 44 warnings it has on `024b7b6`, and the two test files have 0. The config sets no `parserOptions` / `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- Pre-tsc battery, all exit 0: `check:phantom-deps`, `self-import`, `unreferenced-sources`, `doc-example-readers`, `handler-key-reads`, `side-effects-array`, `element-data-source-declaration`, `spec-symbols`, `action-forward-parity`, `designer-field-key-parity`, `icon-record-names`, `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift`, `i18n-designer-parity`, `control-bytes`, `vi-mock-inherit`, `vi-mock-specifiers`, `vi-mock-override-shape`, `test-path-roots`, `new-line-citations`, `scripts/check-hand-rolled-comment-mask.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`.
- Changeset `.changeset/12980-route-chunk-preload.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`. No exported member is added: the new helpers are module-local to `AppContent.tsx`, and the package barrel exports only `AppContent`.

## Acceptance notes

- The dashboard route's residual (87–147 ms after chrome commit in this rig) is the dashboard chunk graph still loading. It might shrink if the import started before `AppContent` mounts (for example, from the URL at console boot), but that is outside this claim's surface. Noted, not done.
- `index.ts` describes "the six `lazy()` declarations `AppContent` writes for" the metadata admin. They are now spelled `routeChunk.lazy(...)`, which reads the same way to the ledger. The prose was not changed.
